newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Box position rolls out to Dec.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Box position rolls out to Dec.

text.p: A big trade in a typically sleepy index option was a highlight in an otherwise moderate session of index options trading.
A box position in the American Stock Exchange's institutional index was rolled out from the June expiration and up from the 775/800 strike price, traders and analysts said.
The XII June 775 and 800 calls and puts each traded 12,000 contracts, as did the December 900 and 925 calls and puts.
The XII spot index was about 4-1/2 points higher at 950.70 in late trade.
On Tuesday, the XII reached a record high of 952.74.
"I have a hunch (the investor) closed the Junes and moved to the Decembers," said Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co, noting that open interest in the June contracts was high.
Open interest in the June 775 and 800 calls was exactly 12,000. In the June 775 puts it was 12,100, and in the June 800 puts it was 13,400.
"It looks like the bulk of the open interest was a box," said Michael Schwartz, a managing director at Oppenheimer & Co.
He said the roll was probably done by a market maker, as the XII options are not often busy.
Open interest in the December 900 and 925 puts was 30 contracts each. It was just two in the December 925 calls. The December 900 calls had no open interest.
A box position is basically a long call and short put at one exercise price and a short call and long put at another exercise price.
A short call/long put position is basically a synthetic short underlying position and a long call/short put position is a synthetic long position.
The XII is made up of 76 of the largest institutional holdings, including AT&T Corp, Chrysler Corp General Electric Co and Philip Morris Cos Inc.
In other activity, a large one-by-four put spread crossed in S&P 500 index options at the Chicago Board Options Exchange, traders said.
The SPX June 825 put traded 41,630 contracts and the July 815 put traded 11,115.
"Today we had one June/July ratio spread," said an index trader. "They were selling the June out-of-the-money and buying the July out-of-the money puts on a smaller ratio."
The SPX was up 4.37 at 869.64 in late trading Wednesday. June S&P 500 futures were up 2.60 at 871.30.
The trader said a large British bank had done the put spread in the SPX.
Other than that big trade, dealers said activity was relatively quiet as the market bounced around.

"We're twiddling our thumbs wondering if the market's going to continue its movement on the upside," the SPX trader said, noting that some economic data due out later this week could shake the market up.
